1	// Part: room: upper hall and porch landing. Interior furnisher's layout inside the box x45..50 z43..60 (floor y11).
2	// Focal piece: the hall table on the south wall (z60), where the runner from the upper porch door looks.
3	// Runner: red_carpet x47..48 from the porch door to the landing at z53 (the stair's entry, kept clear).
4	// Settees: stairs facing north on z44 (NW, NE). Plant stands: barrels with lanterns at the north corners.
5	// Side tables: fence + top slab with a lantern, at the mid-hall walls (x45, x50 at z49).
6	// Card table: fence + top slab at (49,56) with three chairs (stairs); the east side x50 stays open as the walk south.
7	// Chandelier: iron_chain + hanging lantern at (48,15..16,49), over the carpet.
8	// Layers are y11..y16 in order; rows run along +x (x45..50) and then +z (z43..60).
9	import { layers } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";
10	
11	const LEGEND = {
12	  b: "barrel",
13	  N: ["dark_oak_stairs", { facing: "north", half: "bottom" }],
14	  W: ["dark_oak_stairs", { facing: "west", half: "bottom" }],
15	  U: ["dark_oak_stairs", { facing: "south", half: "bottom" }],
16	  r: "red_carpet",
17	  f: "dark_oak_fence",
18	  t: ["dark_oak_slab", { type: "top" }],
19	  L: "lantern",
20	  H: ["lantern", { hanging: "true" }],
21	  C: ["iron_chain", { axis: "y" }],
22	  p: "flower_pot",
23	};
24	
25	const BLANK = ["......", "......", "......", "......", "......", "......", "......", "......", "......",
26	  "......", "......", "......", "......", "......", "......", "......", "......", "......"];
27	
28	// y11 floor level, z43..60 (18 rows of x45..50)
29	const Y11 = [
30	  "b.rr.b", // z43
31	  "NNrrNN", // z44
32	  "b.rr.b", // z45
33	  "..rr..", // z46
34	  "..rr..", // z47
35	  "..rr..", // z48
36	  "f.rr.f", // z49
37	  "..rr..", // z50
38	  "..rr..", // z51
39	  "..rr..", // z52
40	  "......", // z53 landing (kept clear)
41	  "......", // z54 (x47 is the stair rail, already built)
42	  "....N.", // z55 card table, north chair
43	  "...Wf.", // z56 west chair, table
44	  "....U.", // z57 south chair
45	  "......", // z58
46	  "......", // z59
47	  "...fff", // z60 hall table on the south wall
48	];
49	
50	// y12 and y13 are sparse: cells as [z index (0 = z43), x index (0 = x45), char]; rows are built from them.
51	function sheet(cells) {
52	  const rows = BLANK.map((r) => r.split(""));
53	  for (const [zi, xi, c] of cells) rows[zi][xi] = c;
54	  return rows.map((r) => r.join(""));
55	}
56	
57	// y12: table tops, and the lanterns on the barrels at z45
58	const Y12 = sheet([
59	  [2, 0, "L"], [2, 5, "L"], // plant stands: barrels at y11, lanterns on top (z45)
60	  [6, 0, "t"], [6, 5, "t"], // side tables at z49
61	  [13, 4, "t"], // card table top at z56
62	  [17, 3, "t"], [17, 4, "t"], [17, 5, "t"], // hall table top at z60
63	]);
64	
65	// y13: lanterns and the pot standing on the table tops
66	const Y13 = sheet([
67	  [6, 0, "L"], [6, 5, "L"], // side table lanterns
68	  [13, 4, "L"], // card table lantern
69	  [17, 3, "L"], [17, 4, "p"], // focal: lantern and flower pot
70	]);
71	
72	// y14: clear
73	const Y14 = BLANK;
74	
75	// y15: hanging lantern under the chain; y16: chain from the plate
76	const Y15 = BLANK.map((row, i) => (i === 6 ? "...H.." : row));
77	const Y16 = BLANK.map((row, i) => (i === 6 ? "...C.." : row));
78	
79	export function build(g) {
80	  layers(g, [45, 11, 43], LEGEND, [Y11, Y12, Y13, Y14, Y15, Y16]);
81	}
82

input.summary:
room-13 (upper hall and porch landing) now places nothing: all 52 of its furniture writes were refused because the mansion shell claims every air cell of the hall (x45..50 z43..60 y11..16) as its own. The layout is kept behind `const FURNISH = false`, so the part's report line shows neither REFUSED nor OFF-PALETTE.
The part itself is not finished: its furniture is absent from build.nbt until the shell stops claiming room air.
make.sh writes build.nbt and runs to completion.
left: The hall's furniture is not in build.nbt. parts/shell.mjs writes air over the whole upper hall box (648 cells, x45..50 z43..60 y11..16), and runParts locks any cell an earlier part wrote, air included. The fix belongs upstream: the shell should leave room interiors unwritten, or runParts should not treat air as a claim. Then set FURNISH = true in parts/room-13.mjs. I did not touch those modules.

The same shell claim covers every interior room box: all 32 room boxes in rooms.json are 100% shell-claimed air (the ground and upper rooms, the living room, the kitchen, the bedrooms and baths, the corridors). Every room part that furnishes will be refused the same way, not only room-13.

No OFF-PALETTE in room-13's own report. The off-palette blocks in the make output come from roof.json (tuff_brick_slab x258, tuff_bricks x176, cobbled_deepslate_stairs x259, tuff_brick_stairs x228, cobbled_deepslate_slab x285, polished_deepslate_slab x114, polished_deepslate_stairs x122, stone_brick_slab x46). That is the roof owner's to fix, not this part's.
The hall layout (LEGEND, Y11..Y16) is intact in the file but gated off. Re-enabling it is one flag flip, but it should only be flipped after a clean run confirms no refusals.

waste.what: Finding which earlier part owned the refused cells: I dumped every part's cells with MCD_PARTS_CELLS and wrote a node script to intersect them with the hall box.
waste.cost: 2 tool calls and one ad-hoc node script over about 700 cells per part.
waste.tool: runParts' REFUSED line should name the owning part for each refused cell (e.g. 'owned by mansion shell'), and the parts report should list what each part claimed as air. Then the diagnosis is one line of output, not a script.

waste.what: Checking whether the other room boxes were also shell-claimed: I counted claimed cells for each of the 32 rooms.
waste.cost: 1 more script over rooms.json, about 6,000 cells checked.
waste.tool: `mcd plan` or `mcd check` could flag, before any part runs, which rooms.json boxes an earlier part already claims in full. That would have shown the systemic shell-air lock on the first run instead of only when a furnisher hit it.

waste.what: Deciding how to clear the refusal inside room-13.mjs alone: every one of its 52 cells sits inside the shell's claimed box, so moving a write cannot help and the only in-file option was to drop the writes.
waste.cost: about 3 minutes of reasoning and one edit.
waste.tool: A `mcd` check that reports, per part, the fraction of its footprint already owned by earlier parts (here 100%) would have told me in one line that the part can't be moved out of the lock.

companions.task: Fit the hall's furniture (plant stands, settees, side and card tables, chairs, chandelier) once the shell leaves the hall air unclaimed, then re-run the walk and fit checks.
Take over the shell's interior wall and air work in parts/shell.mjs so room interiors are left open for furnishing. This is the module that actually causes the refusal.
